Did the Serb attacks on your area cease on the 6th of August, 1992? But before you respond to my question, we are making very slow progress and I kindly ask you to give us very concise answers. My question to you was whether the attacks ceased on the 6th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Quite the contrary; they intensified.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us precisely what was attacked?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Region of Susnjari, Brezova Njiva, Glogova, Jaglici, and Konjevic Polje. I apologise. All the way across Potocari, with long-range artillery.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us: Do you remember what happened on the 8th of August, 1992, if anything happened at all?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 8th of August, 1992 was my second birthday. During the night, and in the morning, the enemy artillery fire intensified from all directions; from Rogac, Kravica, Brezik, Jezestica, Lipenovici, Kajici. In the early morning hours, an infantry attack was launched on Jaglici, Brezova Njiva, Susnjari, in my area, and followed by that, then fire was opened from all different weapons, so that the ground itself was on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find out what the objective of these attacks was?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't hard to find out that the objective was to seize the area of Lupoglav, Ravni Buljim, Susnjari, what was my area, and thereby to seize control of the entire region.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You described the artillery attacks for us, as far as I understood. Were there any infantry attacks on that day?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From all the directions; from Lipenovici, Jezestica, Djermani, Veresinje, all the way in the direction of Bukova Glava, or rather, across Bukova Glava, and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness mentioned another name of the locality. The interpreter didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, up to what point did the Serbian artillery come?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because there is one locality missing in the transcript. Lipenovici, Jezestica, Djermani, Bukova Glava, and which other place did you mention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Veresinje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the direction of Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Up to what point did the Serbian army come in the area of Susnjari and Jaglici?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of Lupoglav, I believe they came within 200 metres of Lupoglav, and I'm talking about the infantry forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you have the impression that something was going on in the vicinity of your area? Did you hear about something happening?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime after noon, I heard that there was fierce fighting in the Veresinje plateau, in Cizmici, Bukova Glava, Hajducko Groblje, and Ravna Gora, from the direction of Siljkovici and Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And how did you find that out?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat that I had my Motorola on me. And I listened in to the Serbian side mentioning Veresinje, because they were panic-stricken. There was an attack from Cizmici and Golici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you situated at the time?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Lupoglav, the highest elevation point from which I could hear, listen in to all that was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you notice and observe in the area of Lupoglav in the course of the 8th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my vantage point, I could see the Jezestica plateau and two columns of smoke rising from two different localities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please describe for the Trial Chamber what Stara Jezestica is, what sort of a locality that is. Perhaps you could use the map that we referred to yesterday.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can explain. In front of me there is Djermani, to the north, and then there is Stara Jezestica, and this is an area that falls under Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have I understood you well: There is an old part of Jezestica and a new part?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where is Stara Jezestica situated, the old part?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between Djermani and Nova Jezestica, or rather Kajici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that on the hill or in the valley?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have described the course of the attack which lasted the entire morning, and I meant the attack against your area.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a lull in the fighting at a certain point; and if so, why?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Around noon, the infantry fire subsided in my area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ademovic, please allow a short interval of time between question and answer, because I can feel that the interpreters are finding it difficult to catch up with you, or keep with the pace, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think that this was not entered into the record: Why do you think that there was a lull in the fighting, or rather, did you have any information to the effect that the attack against your area subsided? And of course, please try to break -- to make a pause before answering.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was listening in over my Motorola, and I realised that the Serbian side was asking for reinforcements in the area of Veresinje and that the Golici's boys in the area of Cizmici had pushed back the Serbian forces, which were panic-stricken and urgently asking for assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At some point you said that you noticed two columns of smoke rising in Donja Jezestica. Can you please describe this for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were these columns of smoke precisely?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Gornja Jezestica, at one end of the village, and the other -- or rather, two columns of smoke appeared on each side of the village, which was something that I was not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what happened next. Did something happen next?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the direction of Kravica and Bratunac, I could see a stretch of the road there, and I noticed several lorries arriving to assist the forces there. Once the smoke appeared, an intense artillery fire was opened from the area of Brezovik upon Stara Jezestica, upon the houses there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that you noticed several lorries arriving as part of assistance. In assistance to whom?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you notice next? What happened after the artillery attack targeting houses, as you stated?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could see the smoke first, and then the fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were familiar with the area of Stara Jezestica. You stated so yesterday several times. The houses there in Stara Jezestica, they were built of what sort of material?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wood, adobe bricks, and there were several older houses there, but they were mostly made of wood.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Cerpic" in B/C/S is not really a type of a brick, is it? Can you tell the Trial Chamber what it is.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is basically soil which has not been in a kiln, has not been really baked, but I believe that people familiar with these materials would know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. During the day did you find out exactly what was happening and who was fighting in the area of Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shortly after the artillery opened fire, I thought that the Muslims had entered the area and that the artillery was there to push them out of the area. I also thought that the assistance that I saw arriving was meant for that area and for the area of Veresinje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the attack, did anybody come to your village?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon hours, when the fighting subsided, I saw men arriving wearing uniforms that I saw for the first time. There were several of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know these people?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was because we knew each other that Safet Hodzic, from Hranca, came to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again, no objection, just an issue of clarification in order to follow the evidence. The witness said: "Shortly after the artillery opened fire ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. "I thought that the Muslims had entered the area and that the artillery was there to push them out of the area. I also thought that the assistance that I saw arriving was meant for that area and for the area of Veresinje."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sorry. I meant the next line. Question: "After the attack, did anybody come to your village?" Answer: "In the afternoon, when the fighting subsided." The witness has given extensive evidence about Stara Jezestica and Donja and Gornja Jezestica and other villages in the area. Are we to understand that to be a reference to generalised fighting in the whole area or in a specific village? Perhaps, for example, Jezestica or part of it. It's not insignificant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree with you, and it will be more practical to deal with it now rather than you take it up on cross-examination. So if you could address this question to the witness directly. Or you have heard what Mr. Di Fazio has said. Perhaps you can enlighten us on this, what you mean exactly, which area you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant Jezestica, Stara Jezestica, and Djermani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify the following: You meant Stara Jezestica and Djermani, but what exactly did you have in mind, that the fighting subsided over there or that the fighting subsided in your area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That the fighting subsided in my area, whereas the fighting was still going on in Veresinje and in the direction of Cizmici. Do I need to explain any further?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I have put a question to you, and please listen closely to the questions I put to you. The fighting that you have described as having subsided in your area, for how long did they still go on in the area of Veresinje and Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the late afternoon, evening hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned these men as having arrived in these uniforms. When exactly did they come to your area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon, between 3.00 and 4.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You were going to tell us something about Hodzic Safet, hailing from Hranca. Was there somebody else in that group with him?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Safet is a relative of mine. There was Hakija Malic, from Donja Potocari with him there, and another friend of mine of a long time, Dzemo Tihic, from Skelani, the brother of Ahmo Tihic, if that name means something to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell us: Who were these men? Apart from the fact that you knew them from before the war, were they members of a structure at the time?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were men who arrived in the area of Konjevic Polje as members of the 16th Muslim Brigade from Tuzla, under the command of Nurif Rizvanovic, as they told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you this that very day when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I asked them where they were from.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know Nurif Rizvanovic from before?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him well from before the war. He was a military man. He was quite a controversial figure. But I -- everything that I knew about him then was from before the war, from the workplace where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you talk with Hodzic Safet and Dzemo Tihic and Rizvanovic about the entire events on the 8th of August 1992, and what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told me that in early August they arrived in the Konjevic Polje area and that on that day they were in the area of Lolici and the nearby village of Kamenica, and that through their communication devices that they had, they had heard that the Serbian side wanted to seize the area of Jaglici and Susnjari, Lupoglav, and Ravni Buljim.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they mention Siljkovici in connection with that?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. In the area of Siljkovici, the Serb forces had very strong positions, they having heard what was going on, decided to start moving. There were about 400 of them, I believe. One group set out in the direction of Siljkovici, another group in the direction of Jezestica and Djermani.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you have any information about the activities of Ejub Golic's group?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I heard over my Motorola that Golic's men were attacking. That's something that I was able to hear on the channels used by the Serb Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from Ejub Golic's group and Nurif's unit, were you aware of some other Muslim groups participating in the fighting around Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a group from Pale, led by Senad Golubovic, fighting there as well?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I hear about this for the first time now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In these clashes, did the groups from Suceska take part as well, according to what you know about it?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was physically impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the terrain where we were and because of the distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge and according to what Nurif Rizvanovic's men, who arrived, said to you, did they have any losses in the fighting of that day? Nurif's men, I mean.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to what they said, and I later was able to see this for myself, some of the men who went to Siljkovici had quite a lot of losses, and they were not successful. Because the Serbs were very well fortified there, they quickly received help from Kravica. The group that went in the direction of Jezestica and Djermani also had losses because they clashed with the Serb side in the Hajducko Groblje area, where, according to what they said, and you could see that they were more numerous and better equipped, they pushed the Serb side back through Djermani and entered Stara Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now show the witness Exhibit D647. This is a list of military conscripts sent to the free territory on the 27th July 1992, as part of the 16th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you look at page 7. Count the pages, please. It begins with number 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's on page 9 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if you have found it, look at the name under number 41. Do you see this? The page begins with the number 17. And then under 41, Safet Hodzic, son of Vejsil, from Hranca. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but this is a double list that I have here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Page 7, the seventh page. Have you seen it?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Number 41, Safet Hodzic, son of Vejsil. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the person who you said arrived in Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please turn another three pages, and on page 10 it begins with number 1. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at number 12, Rifeta -- Hakija Malic, son of Rifeta from Potocari. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the person whom you said arrived in Susnjari on that day?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please look at page 13 in the Bosnian version, the name before the last.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Your Honours, may I draw your attention to the fact that this is page 17 in English, and there is an error in translation here. That's why I would like the usher to put it on the ELMO. The name is Dzemo Tihic, son of Mujo, whereas in English it says that this is Bedrija Tihic, son of Dzemo. An error has crept in here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see this, Witness?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's written in pen.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which number is it, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's -- well, it's the name before the last. I think it's number 22, Your Honours. It says here "Tihic, son of Mujo, Dzemo."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It can't be, in fact, so it has to be another page. Can you -- this last page you had on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the English translation, it's under number 1 on page 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is -- the number, it says here Bedrija Tihic, son of Dzemo. This is quite wrong. That's why I'm asking you to look at the Bosnian original. The name before the last, at the bottom, Tihic, Dzemo, son of Mujo. Is that the person who came to your area on that day?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is this the person who you said was Ahmo Tihic's brother?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now please keep this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And would the usher now show the witness D801.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These are photographs of members of the 16th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher show the witness photograph 2 of 3. Can this be put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's better to put it on the ELMO. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be made a bit clearer?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, do you recognise the people on this photograph? If it can be focussed a bit better. It's very blurred on the ELMO. Witness, do you see it?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I know these people well, I can recognise them. But for Their Honours and for your sake ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us: Who is on this photograph? You said you recognised them.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the left of me is Safet Hodzic, and to my right is Huso Rizvanovic, the brother of Mr. Rizvanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who -- or rather, did any of these two people arrive in Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Safet Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at these other two photographs. But before we move on, tell us: Did you discuss with Hodzic the whereabouts of Nurif Rizvanovic and his brother?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I asked him where Nurif Rizvanovic was, and he told me that he had gone with his brother to Cizmici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now please look at these other photographs that we have here. Can you show the witness the other photographs, please. Just take a look and I'll ask you to comment on the uniforms and the caps. And I want to ask you: The people you just mentioned as having arrived in Susnjari, were they wearing the kind of uniforms and caps we see in these photographs?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the first time we had encountered such uniforms and such insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they have this crescent moon and star?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From your experience with the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, did the regular Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina wear such insignia, or rather, did you see such insignia, either in your area or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the first time we had seen such insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you spoke to these men, let's say Hodzic, did you discuss the whereabouts of their command? What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They said they had arrived with Nurif Rizvanovic, that he was their commander, and that they had come from Tuzla, and that their command was in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, from what you learned on that day, did they, in early August 1992 -- were they under the command from someone from Konjevic Polje or someone in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither Konjevic Polje nor Srebrenica. Their commander Nurif was from Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what did they say was the reason of their arrival in the area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To help their people, because most of the people from Podrinje or from Bratunac and Srebrenica -- or rather, most of them came from Podrinje or from Bratunac and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can put away these photographs now. You mentioned that among the group that arrived in Susnjari was also Dzemo Tihic. Did I understand you correctly to say that you knew him well before the war?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you talk with him on that day?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you talk about? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked, as I said, about those two; where they were from, who they were, what they were, and he insisted on being told where his brother might be and how he could contact him. That's Ahmo Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you discuss these uniforms with these men?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We liked the uniforms. We thought they were very interesting. And I wanted Dzemo, my friend, to lend me one of those uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did anyone in Susnjari have uniforms before that time?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what did Dzemo tell you about the uniform?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He took out a uniform from his backpack and showed it to me, but he said it was a gift for his brother, Ahmo Tihic, and that he couldn't give it to me, but that he would try to get one for me from one of his friends. However, I never did receive a uniform from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find out whether Ahmo's brother managed to reach Ahmo?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Very soon after that, and he remained in Srebrenica until the fall of Srebrenica, and that is, until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I now wish to have a video played. It's P433, the part that begins at 54:39. It's a very brief video clip.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] I know that best. In Skelani --"

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just hang on a second. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this person, first of all?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Ahmo Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Take a good look at the uniform here. Is this a uniform like the one you saw that day, that Nurif's men had, including the one shown to you by Ahmo Tihic's brother, or the one he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the uniform they wore, the uniform brought by the lads from Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they all have the same insignia on those uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The insignia were of different sizes, but they were lilies. However, they were of different sizes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before Nurif's men arrived in your area, did you see uniforms in other Muslims groups in the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not like these. Sometime around the 12th of April, or the 20th of April --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. The 20th of April of what year?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can continue now.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While -- before my area was physically cut off, around the 20th of April, I met Mr. Oric and I saw him in a similar uniform, but not identical to these, and there were four or five men with him. The uniforms were quite different.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to discuss this uniform with Oric, and did you ask him where he got it from?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I asked him and his lads - there were five or six of them - and they said that they had taken these uniforms from Arkan's men when they set an ambush for them in Potocari. They took those uniforms and some ammunition. There was a 53, a sniper, light infantry weapons, and so on, and they took those uniforms from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "took," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took them off the bodies of dead soldiers, and from a vehicle that had been damaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there other fighters who got hold of uniforms in the same manner?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this happened very rarely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the demilitarisation, was this the only way, except for the uniforms brought along by Nurif's men, was this the only way to obtain uniforms, or did you get them from somewhere?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only way was the way I've described. There was no other way. Sometimes one could make a uniform from some tarpaulin left over by the former JNA, but this also was very rare.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From what you saw when you arrived in Srebrenica, how many men had uniforms? Was it a small number, a large number? How would you describe it?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A small number of men had uniforms. It was mostly these lads who had arrived from Tuzla with Mr. Rizvanovic, who wore uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether they had any kind of nickname?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were called Nurif's men.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Any other nickname connected to the colour of their uniform, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were called Arkan's men, Naser's men, Sidik's men, Zulfo's men, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. I meant something to do with uniform, but it doesn't matter. We'll move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have another video played now. It's P318, the first of two videos, the part that begins at 0018 to 0021.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can stop it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, do you recognise anyone here?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you take a look at his uniform.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a uniform that was worn by Arkan's and Seselj's men Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. when, on the 17th of April, 1992, there was an ultimatum and there were talks in Fontana. This is the original uniform. Moreover, I think that Mr. Oric didn't even remove the insignia. I saw something like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This round insignia, or patch, does it have anything to do with the patches you saw worn by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw such patches only in Bratunac, and I remember them well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the uniform you saw Oric wearing when you said you met him around the 20th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. I can never forget that uniform, because the first time I felt fear and terror was when I saw men wearing these uniforms in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, this uniform worn by Oric did not have any other specific insignia apart from the ones you saw on the 20th?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'll now move on to another topic. Following these events in August 1992, how did the situation develop in the area of Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I've moved on to a different topic. After the events described by you in August 1992, before we moved on to these questions about the uniforms, do you remember what was going on after the 8th of August, 1992? The situation in the area of Susnjari, how did it develop?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation deteriorated. The fighting intensified. There were ever greater numbers of the refugees. However, we managed to physically become connected with Brosevici, so we lifted the blockade partially. And the refugees started leaving in the direction of Bljeceva. But the situation in terms of the health conditions and food was terrible. And the artillery and infantry attacks did not cease fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show D764 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document issued by the command of the Bratunac garrison, dated 11 October 1992. The number is 04336999. I will quote item 1. Do you have the document before you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Item 1 indicates: "Together with the forces from Kravica, we have laid strong ambushes." And then look at points 3, 4, 5, where it says: "We established communications according the Kravica plan. The line held by the Kravica forces has not shifted towards Konjevic Polje but remains where it was before. Sopotnik, Lupoglava, elevation point 661, Banjevici, Gornja Brana, Donja Brana, Neradje, Krusik, elevation point 334, Marici, Lazar, Menjak, Kacalovica, Ormice, Jezestica." The Serbian positions in the area around your position, was it as reflected in this document in August 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will quote from paragraph 5 of this document: "The air force attacked during the 10th of October 1992, in the afternoon, and on the 11th of October, 1992, they attacked the forces intervening from Srebrenica." To the best of your knowledge, the aviation, did it fire upon the area where you were, upon your positions, on the 10th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 10th of October 1992 and onwards, around Susnjari, Potocari, the entire area, Glogova, was under attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the witness another document. This is Defence Exhibit D818. This is a document of the command of the Drina Corps, dated 19 November 1992, entitled "The cutting off of the Srebrenica-Cerska corridor, order." I will read to you item 1, where it is stated: "Cut off the Srebrenica-Cerska corridor on the general axis along the Kravica, Rogac villages."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you have the larger map that we used yesterday, if you have it before you.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is map D841.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it could be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please show the Trial Chamber the entire area of the village of Kravica on the map. Therefore, not the very centre of the village of Kravica but all of the inhabited areas coming under the village of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Kravica covers a wider area. The local commune embraces some 20 to 25 villages, including Jezestica, Siljkovici, Veresinje, Konjevic Polje -- I apologise. Kajici, Brezik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you roughly encircle the area with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please show the area of Rogac for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The entire area.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Including Koprivno, up to Koprivno.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What -- in what way would this cutting off the Srebrenica-Cerska corridor affect Susnjari and your area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would mean that we would be physically cut off from Konjevic Polje and it would be connected with the military forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What sort of meaning did it have for you in Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would mean that we would be entirely cut off from Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have told us that up to that point, the refugees were able to move between your area and Konjevic Polje, although there were some of them who suffered as casualties. But what does this order mean for you?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It meant preparations for the total destruction of my area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at point 3 of the document, as follows: "The commanders of the Birac and Bratunac Light Brigades are duty-bound to organise direct and full coordination and work out a plan of coordinated action." In the second half of November 1992, did you in Susnjari know about the coordinated action and possible large-scale attacks against your area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I've said, I was able to follow the developments through my police Motorola. I fully understood what was going on and I had the information. I was also able to follow visually what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you inform anyone thereof, anyone who was close to your positions?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The leader of the group from Jaglici and Brezovik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did it cause panic in your area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only panic, but fear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally try to reach Srebrenica to inform them of the situation in your area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Around the 24th of November, I believe it was, that I went to Srebrenica, to the municipality building, where I tried to explain the situation on the ground in terms of food, accommodation and manpower, and to tell them what lay in store for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you try to obtain help from them?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you talk to over there?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to certain groups in Srebrenica and the representatives of the Srebrenica Presidency, Senad [as interpreted], who was then standing for Abdic, because I was late for that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said "Senahid" rather than "Senad," as it was entered into the transcript. Do you know this man? What's his last name?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Senahid hails from Skenderici, Stozerska, and that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Naser Oric was there? You know him well. Did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. According to the information I obtained that day, Naser Oric was not there. That same day, there were very strong infantry, artillery attacks upon the area of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Slow down, because I am sure, for example, that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Slow down, please, because I'm sure that part of your question, previous question, for example, was not even translated in time for him to answer. You had asked him for the last name of Senahid, and you can see from his answer that he never got that part of the question interpreted for him. And the reason is that he is immediately answering before you have even finished your question. So, Mr. Ademovic, if you don't want to get more angry looks from the interpreters' booths, please slow down and allow an interval, a very short interval of time, and allow Ms. -- not just Ms. Vidovic to finish, but allow the interpreters to translate to us in English, and to others in French, what has been stated by Ms. Vidovic. Because otherwise, we will never get there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember Senahid's last name?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tabakovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tabakovic. Thank you very much. You indicated that you had sought assistance from the people in Srebrenica and from representatives of other armed groups, in view of the difficult situation you were in. Did you ever get the assistance?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From that point onwards, did your situation grow ever more difficult?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in every respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the witness a document issued by the command of the Drina Corps, number 04358083, dated 13th December 1992, wherein it is stated: "The execution of the combat linking up between Sekovici and the command of the Bratunac Brigade." It was issued by Colonel Milenko Zivanovic to the command of the Bratunac Brigade. The number is, as I said, 04358083, and I will quote the first part of the document, Mr. Ademovic, please. It is stated here: "Because of linking up the combat schedule in the village of Koprivno, Manovici, Brezanci, Siljkovici, you should organise for your commanding officer, or several commanding officers, to arrive on the 14th of December, 1992, at 9.00, in the village of Manovici, where they will be joined by the commander of the Milici battalion units. They are also duty-bound to agree in detail on the organisation of the combat line."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This part of the document I read out for you, according to your experience, is that the realisation of the order of the Drina Corps of the 19 December of 1992 to cut off the corridor along Kravica-Birac?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I just look at the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You can look at the villages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The village of Manovici, Brezanci, Siljkovici. At Brezanci and Siljkovici, the forces linked up physically and these were the villages from which we were constantly attacked.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, these were Serbian villages?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Serbian villages directly contiguous to my area of Susnjari, Ravni Buljim, and Jaglici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document, consisting of two pages, the one B/C/S having ERN number 0458083, and the next page being the corresponding translation thereof into English, is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D848.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have the usher's assistance in showing a new document to the witness. This is a document by the Milici garrison command, dated 14 December 1992. This is an order by the commander, Bosko Sargic, addressed to the command of the Birac Brigade, number 04337183. And I will quote a part of the document. A part of item 2. It is stated: "Reconnaissance of the area towards Kravica was completed on our side, but the troops from Kravica did not come to the rendezvous, probably for justified reasons. We sent a letter by courier to Kravica and proposed the following: We should set up ambushes by 1200 hours on the 15th of December, 1992. The line of contact with Kravica should be the village of Bare in the Kravica area. The ambush commander on our side should be Blagoje Vidovic. The ambush should be set up along the line Manovici village, Crvanj stream, Brezanci village, across the trig point BTT1, then via Boksin Potok up to Bare and further on. The men from Kravica should continue from Bare via Hajducko Groblje to Siljkovici. We are requesting agreement from the Kravica men and the brigade and then we can start carrying out the task. Communication and artillery have not been planned because we have not met to agree on this point."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The villages mentioned in this document, the villages of Manovici, Crvanj Potok, Brezanci, are these the villages neighbouring your area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what was going on in mid-December 1992 in your area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in mid-December 1992, the circle began to tighten around my area and there was an intense planned and systematic artillery attack on the area of Susnjari, Jaglici, and Brezova Njiva, Cizmici, Velika Glogova, all the way down to Birac, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, while this was going on, were those thousands of refugees you spoke about still with you?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had nowhere to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may this exhibit be given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic. This document, which consists of one page in B/C/S, with ERN 04337183, and the other page being the -- containing the corresponding translation thereof into English, is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D849.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now please show the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. witness D821.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document issued by the Bratunac Brigade Command. It's dated the 15th of December, 1992. The title is "Reply to telegram." It's addressed to the Drina Corps commander and sent by Lieutenant Colonel Borivoje Tesic. The document bears the number 04361565. I will quote to you the first part of this document, which says: "This is to inform you that, in order to ensure the link-up of combat dispositions of units along the Koprivno village, Manovici village, Brezanci village, Siljkovici village axis, this is to inform you that Officer Jovan Nikolic, also known as Jole, went to Manovici village to discuss the matter with an officer from Milici." In connection with this, do you know who Jovan Nikolic, also known as Jole, is and where he's from?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Jovan Nikolic, also known as Jole, was from Kravica. He was a teacher there. But at that time, he was a commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This village of Manovici, where, according to the document, this meeting took place, how far is it from the positions you held near Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my position to Rogaci, it's between three and four kilometres as the crow flies, and midway is about two kilometres as the crow flies, so Their Honours can work it out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the village of Manovici, how far is it from your position?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two kilometres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to what you experienced, was there a physical link-up between the Milici and Kravica troops in order to isolate the area of Susnjari, as well as Srebrenica and Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now show the witness a document. The title is "List of persons in military post, 2465/5, who have been paid compensation for official trips and paid for November 1992-infantry battalion." The document is 01397801 to 01319796. And before we go on to discuss this document, I wish to ask you whether you had any knowledge that during November 1992, the Bratunac Brigade had been formed.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know what the position of the Kravica troops was in that brigade?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Through the means of communication I had, that is, my Motorola, I heard it mentioned as the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now please take a look first at page 1, where it says "3rd infantry battalion command." Look at the names here: Milan Milanovic, Nikolic Jovan, Krsto Cvjetinovic, and Nedjo Nikolic. These are numbers 1, 2, 3, and 4. Did you know any of these men?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Jovan Nikolic, Major Nikolic, also known as Djedura.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where were these people from?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now please look at the part where it says "1st Infantry Company." This is a very clear document. Do you know the names? Do you recognise the names on this list? For instance, look at numbers 22 to 29 on the next page.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eric is from the centre of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know them?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Ilic family were from Kravica. They had moved there from Magasici, from Magasici, the area above Jezestica, in the Veresinje area. Zoran Ilic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What number is he here? Is that number 29?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now please turn another page. To save time, look where it says "2nd Infantry Company," on page 4.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are family names from the general area of Kravica, from the periphery of Kravica; Brezik, Popovici, Mandici, towards Glogova Mountain, to the north of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the original, it says "2nd Infantry Company," whereas here it's being translated as "detachment." I think it should be "company" rather than "detachment." And the interpreters can confirm.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see, Witness, that it says 1st and 2nd Infantry Company?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see it says the 2nd Infantry Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And where did you say these people were from? Whom do you know personally?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the Gavrics.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For example, Panto Gavric, son of Krste, where is he from?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's from the village of Gavrici, near Popovici -- the village of Mandici, Mandici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now turn to the next page and look at the numbers from 214 to 219. Do you know the Vasiljevics?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Vasiljevics were from the Brezik area, from Avdagina Njiva on the plateau towards Mandici and Popovici. That's the area where there are some dispersed hamlets, bigger and smaller ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know Pavle Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in order not to waste time, please move to the next page, where it says "3rd Infantry Company," and look at these names.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These names are from the general area of Jezestica, from Veresinje, Rankovici, Radovici, Kajici, Donje and Gornje, that is Stara Jezestica, and Djermani, all the way to Siljkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, for example, look at the name under 353. It's on the next page. Gajo Mladjenovic, son of Nedje, did you know him?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was a neighbour of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where is he from?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know Milenko Trisic, son of Slavoljuba?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Trisics were from Jezestica, both Donja and Gornja, both old and new Jezestica, and these were two twin brothers. Their father's name is Slavoljuba. And one of them is employed in the Bratunac police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now look at the independent platoon, Donji Bacici. Did you know that there was a unit in Bacici?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All these are local people from Bacici. They had a platoon. I know all these names.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now look at the next page. This is the mortar platoon.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise. There's also a Banjevici platoon here, and this is from my village. I know it well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Look at the next page, please, where it says "Mortar platoon, 82-millimetre mortar platoon." Have you found it? Have you found this? The computer number is 01319789, and it's right under Donji Bacici, on the next page. Have you found it? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between Donji and Gornji Bacici there's a mortar platoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but do you see here on the paper where it says "Mortar platoon"? Please don't misunderstand me as suggesting that it was there in that area. It's what it says here on this document, "Mortar platoon, 82 millimetres," and it appears that there are 25 names here. Do you know that during 1992, or rather, do you know where in 1992 the Kravica forces artillery positions were?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the Brezik area. That is the plateau, where you can position a larger number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And where else? Can you make your replies brief. Can you tell us where?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brezik and Rogac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you know whether the Serbs had any weapons in the areas of Banjevici or Bacici?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what they had there?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mortar artillery, tanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now please look further in this document. Did you know that there was a unit in Gornji Bacici?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Turn the page, please. You mentioned knowing that there was an independent platoon or a unit in Banjevici?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now turn the page, where it says the Lipenovici Independent Platoon. In your testimony you mentioned Lipenovici more than once. Please have a look at this list. Do you know the men listed as belonging to the Lipenovici Independent Platoon?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were close neighbours of mine, and they were holding the lines in the Buljim area. The elevation was 820. It was called Ravni Buljim. I apologise, but please, let's clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us whom precisely you know from this list?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milenko Cvjetinovic, Milo Jovanovic, Dragomir Milicevic, Radovana Radoje, son of Radovan Pavlovic. Radovan, son of Cvijetina Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You need not go on. I just wanted to ask you whether you knew about the existence of this platoon throughout 1992, from the beginning of the war onwards?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were at the front lines, holding those lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now turn to the next page, please. Do you see that it says here "volunteers"? Please take a look at this list. It says "volunteers." And look at these last names. You told us that, as a policeman, you visited this area, that you knew the area well, as well as the people there. These last names listed as volunteers, are these local men? Do you know them? Or are these last names which were not prevalent in the area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only one I know is Jovanovic. All the others are unfamiliar names in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Witness, according to this document, one would say that the Kravica Battalion, or rather, the 3rd Infantry Battalion, in November 1992, had at least 600 soldiers in Kravica and its hamlets. Does this correspond to what you knew about the manpower levels of this battalion at this time, in November 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, may this document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. This document, which consists of 32 pages, 16 in B/C/S and 16 in English, with ERN 01319781 to 796, both numbers included, is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D850.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have the usher's assistance now in showing the witness the Defence Exhibit D380. This is a document of financial nature. It is a payment order to be transferred by the 3rd Kravica Battalion, dated 8 December 1992, and the number is 02065934. And I will quote: "As ordered by the account holder, Bratunac municipality budget, transfer of funds for the expenses of the 3rd Kravica Battalion as per the conclusion of the IO."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does Kravica form part of the Bratunac municipality?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on your experience, if someone were to claim that the Kravica forces were not linked up with the Army of Republika Srpska in the area, nor assisted by the Serbian army, would that be true, based on what you know?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Quite the opposite. They were organised and linked up.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, does this document confirm that the 3rd Battalion was financed from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can set this document aside, Mr. Ademovic, and I will now turn to the situation around the 15th of December, 1992, when, as you've said, you were isolated by the Kravica and Milic units from Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher show another document to the witness. This is document 04306275, which is a request from the command of the Bratunac Brigade, dated 15 December 1992, for materiel to be provided, including jet fuel, aerial bombs -- 100 aerial bombs, to be precise. Do you have the document? It is stated: "Pursuant to the request of the Bratunac Brigade command, strictly confidential number -- of 15 December 1992, please provide the following materiel: Jet fuel, 25.000 litres, and 100 aerial bombs."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have described for us that you were encircled by the forces that you said were forces from Kravica and Milici. The encirclement, was it supported by air raids against the area of Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was directed against the stretch from Susnjari to Potocari, Fakovici, including Konjevic Polje and Cerska.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the Jaglici and Susnjari area, whether the encirclement there was also supported by air attacks.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it your impression in the field that these units that were attacking you, that they had the support of the aviation from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document be given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. This will become document D851 and consists of two pages, one in B/C/S, one in English, ERN 04306275.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show a new document to the witness. This is a document issued by the Drina Corps Command, dated 15 December 1992, bearing the number 04306258. This is a brief document. Could the witness please take a look at the document. I will quote the document: "Drina Corps Command, to the General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska." You can see that the fifth map is mentioned here, and I will quote: "In the sector of Milica Brdo, near Milic, oil is leaking from a Nora 152-millimetre howitzer and nitrogen is coming out of an HES. Urgent intervention by an artillery mechanic and spare parts and tools are needed. An artillery mechanic is to report to Captain Starcevic in the 5th Map Command and he will take him to the combat position with a representative of the unit."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what sort of an artillery weapon is Nora 152 millimetres. Is this something that you had occasion to experience?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Let me clarify. The Nora howitzer is a very long-range artillery piece that is very powerful. It can easily destroy an entire Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. building.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this time period, including between autumn and the 7th January 1993, was your area ever targeted with such powerful weapon as this particular howitzer?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From June 1992 until the end of the war, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's fine. However, my question focussed specifically on this particular time period.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the document be assigned an exhibit number, and could the usher show the witness another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. In the meantime, this document will become Defence Exhibit D852. It consists of two pages, again one in English and one in B/C/S, ERN 04306258.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe the usher has already distributed Defence Exhibit D772. This is a document by the Bratunac Brigade Command, dated 16th December 1992, addressed to the Drina Corps Command. The document says: "In the course of the night, open artillery fire on the following features: Susnjari, Potocari, Pale, Jaglici, Poloznik, Pirici."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall whether, on the 16th of December, 1992, or thereabouts, there were artillery attacks against primarily Susnjari and Jaglici?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have that large map with you? Would you please show the Trial Chamber the area covered by this order; Susnjari, Potocari, Pale, Jaglici, Poloznik, Pirici. Can you show the Trial Chamber the area.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the way to Pirici. That is practically the entire territory of the municipality of Srebrenica and the free territory of Bratunac -- or rather, Bratunac itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, that entire area?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that from the 16th of December, 1992, the Serbian forces increased their pressure on the entire area? And when I say "the entire area," I mean your area of Susnjari, Jaglici, Brezova Njiva.

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my area as well. However, the thrust of the attack was on Cizmici, Bljeceva, Glogova, and Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information about what was going on in Cizmici and Velika Glogova?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were grave concerns over these attacks because there were large numbers of refugees in that area, especially in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean Velika Glogova?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I meant Velika Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you obtain the information concerning Velika Glogova and Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, through the communication that I had; second, through the refugees who arrived in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say through your communication, does that mean that you learnt it from the Muslims who were able to communicate or from the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From the Serbs. I meant my Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to what you knew, did the Muslims in the area have a Motorola, as you did?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were large numbers of refugees, though, who went out in search of food.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to be of any help in the area at all?

utterances.speaker: SIDIK ADEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to help them by attacking from the direction of Jezestica and Veresinje, but I was unable to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will stop for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. I just had Madam Registrar check how much time you have used already. Stopping now, you've used five hours, 40 minutes. How much more do you require? How much more do you need? I'm asking you because more or less we need to know whether this gentleman is going to need to stay here over the weekend or whether we can send him home on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I hope to be able to finish in the first session tomorrow, therefore, in an hour and a half. I did my best, and I really can't believe that I spent so much time already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And Mr. Di Fazio, I know that the examination-in-chief is not finished yet. Are you optimistic that you would be able to finish your cross by the end of business on Friday?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Cautious optimism, yes. I'm well aware of the issues, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not forcing you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I know that you're not, Your Honours, and I know that and I appreciate that and the Prosecution is grateful to you for that. But it makes no sense to not try and finish before Friday, so I'll do everything I can. I think I'll be able to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope that you understand that we are doing our level best to make it possible for you to go home Saturday, but you are also volunteering much more information than you are asked. So the chances of staying here are quite high. I thank all the staff for overstaying by about five minutes, and we'll meet again tomorrow, again in the afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 27th day of October 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.21 p.m.,
